issues.legal_issue: A court may refuse to accept a reply affidavit tendered after repeated opportunities to file it when accepting it would cause further delay.
material_facts: The government repeatedly obtained adjournments to prepare and file a reply affidavit but did not file one before the applications were heard.
The government’s counsel was absent when the hearing began, and the affidavit was still not ready when counsel later sought another adjournment.
The government tendered its affidavit only after the hearing had proceeded, and accepting it would have required further opportunity for the opposing party to respond.
The government had been told that cancellation of the challenged notification did not resolve the remaining dispute over possession, and it continued to refuse to hand over the lands.
issues.conclusion: The High Court acted within its discretion in refusing to accept the government’s late affidavit; the Supreme Court found no error in that exercise of discretion.
issues.legal_principle: A court may, in its discretion, refuse a belated affidavit where the party had repeated opportunities to file it and accepting it would cause further delay, including by requiring a response from the other party. The Supreme Court identified no statutory provision or earlier case as the basis for this conclusion.

rule.if: appeal_reviewing_procedural_refusal and repeated_opportunities_to_file and affidavit_tendered_late and further_response_would_delay

predicates.appeal_reviewing_procedural_refusal: A party appeals a court’s refusal to accept a reply affidavit in a proceeding.
predicates.repeated_opportunities_to_file: The party obtained repeated opportunities to prepare and file the affidavit but did not do so.
predicates.affidavit_tendered_late: The party tendered the affidavit only after the proceeding had reached or passed its hearing.
predicates.further_response_would_delay: Accepting the affidavit would require further time for the opposing party to respond.

issues.definition: When a party appeals a procedural refusal after repeatedly failing to file an affidavit on time, and accepting it would cause further delay for a response, the refusal to accept the affidavit is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: Untraversed factual assertions in an affidavit may constitute prima facie evidence of the asserted right when the opposing party files no reply affidavit.
material_facts: The respondent’s applications asserted facts supporting his right to possession of lands assigned to deities, including that the lands had been recorded as assigned and that their income had been handled on behalf of the deities.
The government filed no reply affidavit traversing those assertions, despite having opportunities to do so.
The government acknowledged that the absence of a reply affidavit prevented it from advancing a specific ground for challenging the High Court’s judgment.
The High Court ordered the government to hand over possession, and the government appealed that order.
issues.conclusion: In the absence of a reply affidavit, the High Court was entitled to accept the respondent’s affidavit statements as prima facie evidence of his right to possession; the Supreme Court dismissed the appeals.
issues.legal_principle: Statements made on affidavit that are not traversed by a reply affidavit may constitute prima facie evidence of the asserted facts. Here, the Supreme Court relied on that evidentiary consequence and the government’s inability to identify a specific ground of challenge; it cited no statutory provision or earlier case for this principle.

predicates.appeal_against_possession_order_in_writ_: A party appeals an order made in a writ proceeding directing it to hand over possession of property.
predicates.applicant_asserted_facts_supporting_poss: The applicant made sworn factual assertions supporting a claimed right to possession.
predicates.respondent_filed_no_reply_affidavit: The opposing party filed no reply affidavit traversing the applicant’s sworn assertions.
predicates.appellant_identified_no_specific_challen: On appeal, the appellant could not identify a specific ground challenging the order.

issues.definition: When an appeal against a possession order in a writ proceeding follows untraversed sworn assertions supporting possession and the appellant identifies no specific challenge, the appeal is dismissed and the possession order remains undisturbed.
